stories.hook: ¿Qué antidepresivo funciona mejor en casos graves?
stories.headline: SSRIs y SNRIs son igualmente eficaces, pero los SNRIs reducen más síntomas graves
stories.finding: Diez ensayos y metaanálisis mostraron que SSRIs y SNRIs son eficaces para el trastorno depresivo mayor sin diferencias sustanciales en eficacia global. Sin embargo, los SNRIs (p. ej., venlafaxina, duloxetina) redujeron ligeramente más los síntomas en casos severos, y los SSRIs (escitalopram) tuvieron mejor tolerabilidad y menos interrupciones.
stories.takeaway: Esta evidencia orienta la elección del fármaco según la gravedad y la tolerancia del paciente, favoreciendo SNRIs en depresión severa y SSRIs cuando la tolerabilidad es prioritaria.
stories.paperTitle: COMPARATIVE EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF SSRIS VERSUS SNRIS IN THE TREATMENT OF MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
stories.journal: TPM Testing, psychometrics, methodology in applied psychology
stories.originalAbstract: Background: Major depressive disorder (MDD) remains a significant global health concern, with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) serving as frontline pharmacotherapies. Despite their widespread use, the relative efficacy and tolerability of these classes continue to be debated . Objectives: This systematic review aimed to evaluate and compare the therapeutic efficacy, safety, and remission outcomes of SSRIs and SNRIs across diverse populations, including adults, adolescents, and post-stroke patients with MDD. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, ten randomized controlled trials and meta-analyses were analyzed. Studies included human subjects treated with either SSRIs or SNRIs for MDD, assessing clinical improvement via validated scales such as the HAM-D, MADRS, and CGI-I. Results: Findings consistently indicated that both SSRIs and SNRIs are effective for MDD, with no substantial difference in overall efficacy. However, SNRIs such as venlafaxine and duloxetine showed marginally superior symptom reduction in severe cases, while SSRIs, particularly escitalopram, demonstrated better tolerability and fewer discontinuations due to adverse effects . Conclusions: SSRIs remain the preferred first-line treatment due to their favorable safety and tolerability, while SNRIs are suitable for treatment-resistant or severe depressive episodes. The findings reinforce the need for personalized pharmacological strategies guided by symptom profile, comorbidities, and tolerability.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la terapia metacognitiva superar a la CBT en el síndrome cognitivo-atencional?
stories.headline: La terapia metacognitiva mejora el ajuste social y el PTSD más que la CBT
stories.finding: En un estudio cuasi‑experimental con 45 participantes diagnosticados con síndrome cognitivo‑atencional, se compararon ocho sesiones de terapia metacognitiva, ocho de terapia cognitivo‑conductual y un grupo control sin intervención. La terapia metacognitiva produjo una mejora mayor en el ajuste social y en los síntomas de estrés postraumático que la terapia cognitivo‑conductual.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la terapia metacognitiva puede ser una alternativa más eficaz que la CBT para reducir la rumiación y mejorar la adaptación social en pacientes con síndrome cognitivo‑atencional, orientando la práctica clínica hacia intervenciones que modulen procesos metacognitivos.
stories.paperTitle: Comparison of the Effectiveness of Metacognitive Therapy and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy on Social Adjustment and Post-Traumatic Stress in Individuals with Cognitive-Attentional Syndrome
stories.originalAbstract: The present study aimed to compare the effectiveness of Metacognitive Therapy (MCT) and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) on social adjustment and post-traumatic stress in individuals diagnosed with Cognitive-Attentional Syndrome (CAS) in Tehran during 2023–2024. The sampling method used in this study was simple random sampling, and the research design was quasi-experimental with a pretest-posttest control group structure. The statistical population consisted of all individuals who referred to the counseling centers of the Art and Cultural Organization of Tehran Municipality and were screened as having Cognitive-Attentional Syndrome. A total of 45 participants were selected from this population. Following the completion of pretest questionnaires, two experimental groups participated in eight therapy sessions based on either Metacognitive Therapy or Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, while the control group received no training. Data were analyzed using SPSS-26 software and repeated measures analysis of covariance (ANCOVA). The findings indicated that Metacognitive Therapy, in comparison with Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, led to greater improvement in social adjustment from pretest to posttest and follow-up. However, this result was not observed for post-traumatic stress. Both therapeutic approaches equally reduced post-traumatic stress in participants. The results demonstrated that both Metacognitive Therapy and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy had favorable effects on improving social adjustment and reducing post-traumatic stress. Nonetheless, Metacognitive Therapy proved to be more effective in enhancing social adjustment among individuals with adjustment disorders. In contrast, no significant difference was observed between the two therapies in reducing post-traumatic stress, as both were equally effective.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué la prosopagnosia aumenta la ansiedad social?
stories.headline: Más del 40% de personas con prosopagnosia presentan ansiedad social clínica
stories.finding: En una muestra de 88 personas con prosopagnosia y 58 controles, los primeros obtuvieron una media de 30,25 en la Escala de Ansiedad Social de Interacción, frente a 17,19 en controles. El 44 % de los DPs superó el umbral (vs 14 % controles) y la extraversión se relacionó con menor ansiedad.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo revela que la prosopagnosia conlleva un riesgo significativo de ansiedad social, lo que sugiere la necesidad de evaluar y tratar síntomas ansiosos en esta población, y destaca el papel protector de la extraversión.
stories.paperTitle: Social Interaction Anxiety in Developmental Prosopagnosia: Prevalence, Severity, and Individual Differences
stories.originalAbstract: OBJECTIVE: Although elevated social anxiety in developmental prosopagnosia (DP) has been reported in anecdotal and qualitative studies, the current study sought to better quantify the prevalence, severity, and moderators of social anxiety in a large DP sample. METHOD: A total of 88 DPs and 58 controls completed the validated Social Interaction Anxiety Scale and assessments of face recognition, autism traits, personality (Big Five Inventory), and coping strategies. RESULTS: DPs reported greater social anxiety symptoms (M = 30.25) than controls (M = 17.19), with 44% of DPs above a probable clinical cutoff compared with 14% of controls. Exploratory analyses revealed that DPs' social anxiety was more specific to items pertaining to mixing socially or interacting with unfamiliar people. Notably, several DPs reported minimal social anxiety, which was associated with being more extraverted and having fewer autism traits. A follow-up survey revealed that extraverted DPs more openly disclosed face recognition inabilities than introverted DPs, which may be a factor in their reduced social anxiety. CONCLUSION: These results better quantify the potential serious psychosocial consequences of DP and highlight the importance of individual differences as well as targeted intervention.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la realidad virtual vencer el miedo a las alturas?
stories.headline: La terapia de exposición en realidad virtual con reestructuración cognitiva reduce la acrofobia
stories.finding: En un ensayo controlado aleatorio con 27 participantes, el grupo experimental (n=13) redujo significativamente los puntajes del cuestionario de acrofobia (t(17.08) = -6.173, p<0.05) y la ansiedad del STAI tras seis sesiones. Los cambios fisiológicos mostraron disminución de la frecuencia cardíaca, con menor efecto en conductancia cutánea y respiración.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la combinación de realidad virtual y reestructuración cognitiva es una alternativa eficaz y segura para tratar la acrofobia, ofreciendo mejoras tanto psicológicas como fisiológicas, lo que amplía las opciones terapéuticas para fobias específicas.
stories.paperTitle: Conquer Fear of Heights Using Virtual Reality Exposure Therapy With Cognitive Restructuring
stories.journal: Gadjah Mada Journal of Professional Psychology (GamaJPP)
stories.originalAbstract: Acrophobia has traditionally been treated using exposure therapy; however, virtual reality technology has emerged as an alternative that minimizing security risks by presenting three-dimensional stimuli. This study aimed to investigate virtual reality exposure therapy-cognitive restructuring (VRET-CR) effectiveness in reducing acrophobia symptoms. In a pretest-posttest control group design, 27 participants were randomly assigned to the experimental group (n=13) and the control group (n=14). An independent sample t-test revealed a significant differences in the gain scores of the acrophobia questionnaire (AQ) 1 [t (17.08) = -6.173; p <0.05] and AQ 2 [t (25) = -4.250; p <0.05] between these groups. Scores on the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) and Autonomic Perception Questionnaire (APQ) decreased after six exposure sessions, supporting these findings. Skin conductance and respiratory rate changes during therapy were less significant than heart rate changes. Overall, the results demonstrated the effectiveness of VRET-CR in reducing acrophobia symptoms.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo afecta la interocepción al trauma y la salud mental?
stories.headline: La interocepción deteriorada se asocia con trauma y trastornos mentales
stories.finding: Una revisión de alcance que incluyó 48 estudios encontró que la mayoría reportó interocepción deteriorada en personas con trauma (n=17), trastornos mentales (n=14), trastornos alimentarios (n=10) y problemas de salud relacionados con el estrés (n=7). Estos hallazgos sugieren una relación consistente entre la sensibilidad interoceptiva alterada y diversas condiciones psicológicas.
stories.takeaway: Comprender la alteración interoceptiva como factor transdiagnóstico permite diseñar intervenciones centradas en la conciencia corporal, potencialmente mejorando la regulación emocional en pacientes con trauma y trastornos mentales.
stories.paperTitle: The Relationship Between Interoception and Experiences of Stress, Trauma, and Mental Illness: A Scoping Review
stories.journal: Psychotherapy and Counselling Journal of Australia
stories.originalAbstract: Introduction Interoception—the process of sensing, interpreting, and integrating internal bodily signals—plays a critical role in emotional regulation, behaviour, and wellbeing. In counselling and psychotherapy contexts, impaired interoception is increasingly recognised as associated with how clients experience and respond to stress, trauma, and mental illness. This scoping review aimed to explore the relationship between interoception and these psychological conditions and to determine whether they are associated with heightened (hyper) or reduced (hypo) interoceptive sensitivity. Method A scoping review methodology was used, involving a comprehensive search of four major databases—MEDLINE (Ovid), PsycINFO (Ovid), Embase (Ovid), and CINAHL (EBSCO)—for peer-reviewed articles published between 2014 and October 2024. The screening process included title and abstract screening followed by full text review. Data were synthesised narratively. Results A total of 48 studies were included, covering trauma ( n = 17), mental health conditions ( n = 14), eating disorders ( n = 10), and stress-related physical health issues ( n = 7). Most studies reported impaired interoception across these conditions. Reduced awareness and interpretation of bodily signals (hypo-sensitivity) were more commonly reported than heightened sensitivity, although variability existed across conditions. Conclusion Findings support the relevance of interoception and its relationship to wellbeing in counselling and psychotherapy. In particular, findings suggest that trauma, especially interpersonal trauma, may be associated with clients’ tendencies to avoid bodily awareness, potentially as a protective strategy, and this may co-occur with increased external vigilance. These insights underscore the value of trauma-informed and body-oriented therapeutic approaches. Supporting clients in safely reconnecting with their bodily experiences may enhance emotional regulation and facilitate psychological healing in counselling and psychotherapy settings.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo se entrelazan identificación proyectiva y sesgo hostil?
stories.headline: Identificación proyectiva y sesgo de atribución hostil: una integración teórica inédita
stories.finding: Los autores sostienen que la identificación proyectiva y la proyección son procesos relacionados pero distintos, y que la primera amplía la segunda al inducir respuestas de rol complementarias. Integran estos conceptos con el marco neurocognitivo de Computaciones de Sesgos Hostiles (CHB), ilustrando una viñeta interacción para generar ciclos de agresión.
stories.takeaway: Esta integración brinda a los terapeutas una herramienta conceptual para distinguir entre proyección e identificación proyectiva y comprender cómo los sesgos hostiles pueden alimentar dinámicas agresivas, facilitando intervenciones más precisas en terapia de pareja y en contextos de conflicto interpersonal.
stories.paperTitle: Projective identification, projection and hostile attribution bias in dyadic interactions: some conceptual considerations
stories.originalAbstract: Projective identification plays a central role in psychoanalytic object relations theory and has become a key concept for understanding unconscious interpersonal communication, particularly in psychoanalytic couple therapy. Despite its broad clinical application, conceptual ambiguities remain regarding its distinction from projection and its relationship to contemporary models of social cognition. This paper revisits the concepts of projection and projective identification from an object relations perspective and examines their convergence with the neurocognitive Computations of Hostile Biases (CHB) framework. We argue that projection and projective identification represent related but distinct processes, with projective identification extending projection through the interpersonal induction of complementary role responses. A clinical vignette from psychoanalytic couple therapy illustrates how mutual projective identification and hostile attribution biases interact to produce escalating cycles of aggression, misperception, and role reversals. We suggest that integrating object relations theory with contemporary cognitive models of hostile attribution offers a broader conceptual framework for understanding interpersonal aggression and affect regulation. Such integration may enrich psychoanalytic theory and facilitate dialogue with cognitive neuroscience allowing to improve our theoretical models which inform our therapeutic interventions.

stories.hook: ¿Qué dificultades emocionales impulsan la depresión y ansiedad?
stories.headline: Dificultades para inhibir conductas emocionales predicen depresión y ansiedad
stories.finding: En una muestra de 1,105 adultos, el análisis de redes mostró que la dificultad para inhibir conductas en emociones positivas, la incapacidad de downregular sentimientos negativos y la dificultad para identificar emociones positivas son nodos influyentes. La dificultad para inhibir conductas en emociones negativas se asoció con depresión y ansiedad.
stories.takeaway: Identificar estas dificultades específicas permite diseñar intervenciones focalizadas en la inhibición conductual y la regulación de emociones negativas, mejorando la prevención y el tratamiento de la depresión y la ansiedad.
stories.paperTitle: A network model of affective processes: Links between emotional reactivity, alexithymia, emotion regulation, and their mental health correlates.
stories.originalAbstract: Difficulties in emotion reactivity, awareness (alexithymia), and regulation are highly correlated and feature in a variety of psychological disorders. However, the nature of their connections remains largely unclear. In this study, we applied network analysis to build a network-based model of these three emotional constructs and examined their roles in psychological disorders (depression and anxiety) using data from 1,105 community adults. Participants have been recruited online in 2022. Both undirected networks and directed networks were constructed. The results indicated that difficulty inhibiting behaviors during positive emotions, difficulties downregulating negative feelings, and difficulties identifying positive feelings were highly influential nodes in undirected networks with and without depression and anxiety. Difficulty inhibiting behaviors during negative emotions was most strongly associated with depression and anxiety. The directed network further identified potential driving and outcome nodes among these constructs. These findings advance understanding of the interrelationship between related emotional constructs and their integration within emotional processing. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

stories.hook: ¿Puede un compuesto natural revertir el daño cognitivo por falta de sueño?
stories.headline: Bornyl acetate protege la cognición y reduce la neuroinflamación en ratones privados de sueño
stories.finding: La privación crónica de sueño provocó daño neuronal en el hipocampo y neuroinflamación, deteriorando el aprendizaje y la memoria en ratones. La intervención con bornyl acetate revirtió estos efectos, inhibiendo la vía TLR4/NF‑κB y modificando 29 metabolitos relacionados con vías metabólicas clave.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que el bornyl acetate podría ser una estrategia terapéutica para mitigar el deterioro cognitivo y la inflamación cerebral inducidos por la falta de sueño, abriendo nuevas vías de investigación translacional.
stories.paperTitle: Combined metabolomics and network pharmacology explore the protective mechanism of bornyl acetate against cognitive impairment in chronic sleep-deprived mice
stories.originalAbstract: Abstract Chronic sleep deprivation (CSD) is currently a serious global public health concern, and CSD induces numerous diseases, including cognitive impairment. Bornyl acetate (BA) possesses a brilliant anti-inflammatory activity and plays a favorable role in neuroinflammation. The purpose of this research was to explore the efficacy and the underlying mechanism of BA in cognitive dysfunction caused by CSD. The CSD mouse model was established using a modified multiplatform method. Experimental techniques such as Morris water maze test, tissue staining, western blot, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, metabolomics and network pharmacology were used for the study. The results showed that CSD induced hippocampal neuronal damage and neuroinflammation, leading to impaired learning and memory functions in mice. BA intervention reversed these damages, inhibited neuroinflammation, and improved learning and memory functions in mice, which may be related to the inhibition of TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway. Metabolomics analysis showed that 29 metabolites underwent significant changes after BA intervention, involving arachidonic acid metabolism, glycerophospholipid metabolism, tyrosine metabolism, and glyceride metabolism. Further analyses combined metabolomics and network pharmacology, and 10 core targets on BA modulation of CSD-induced cognitive dysfunction were identified. KEGG enrichment analysis suggested that PPAR signaling pathway, Th17 cell differentiation, Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, Lipid and atherosclerosis, Adipocytokine signaling pathway and Efferocytosis signaling pathway may be important mechanisms by which BA ameliorates CSD-induced cognitive dysfunction. Our study identifies multiple candidate targets and signaling pathways associated with BA against CSD-triggered cognitive dysfunction, which may provide theoretical references for subsequent research on BA and related exploratory strategies.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la autocompasión mejorar la aceptación del dolor?
stories.headline: La autocompasión consciente supera a la TCC en aceptación del dolor crónico
stories.finding: En un ensayo controlado aleatorizado con 61 participantes en MSC y 59 en TCC, la autocompasión consciente generó aumentos mayores en aceptación del dolor y disminuciones de la sensación de indefensión que la TCC. Estos cambios explicaron mejoras en autocompasión, depresión, calidad de vida mental e interferencia del dolor.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que incorporar la autocompasión basada en mindfulness puede potenciar la aceptación del dolor y reducir el sufrimiento, ofreciendo una alternativa más eficaz que la TCC para mejorar la salud mental y funcionalidad en pacientes crónicos.
stories.paperTitle: Shared and Differential Psychological Processes Associated With Treatment Response in Mindful Self‐Compassion and Cognitive‐Behavioural Therapy for Chronic Pain: An Exploratory Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial
stories.originalAbstract: BACKGROUND: Psychological treatments for chronic pain are effective, but the processes associated with therapeutic change, and whether these are shared across treatments or treatment-specific, remain unclear. This exploratory secondary analysis examined whether changes in pain acceptance, pain catastrophizing facets and self-compassion were associated with clinical outcomes in Mindful Self-Compassion (MSC) versus Cognitive-Behavioural Therapy (CBT). METHODS: Data were drawn from a randomized trial comparing MSC (n = 61) and CBT (n = 59) in adults with chronic pain and elevated emotional distress. Processes and outcomes were assessed at baseline and post-treatment. Single and theoretically ordered multiple-mediator models examined whether changes in pain acceptance, rumination, magnification, helplessness and self-compassion were associated with changes in anxiety, depression, quality of life, pain interference and pain intensity. RESULTS: Compared with CBT, MSC produced larger increases in pain acceptance and reductions in helplessness. These processes statistically accounted for improvements in self-compassion, depression, mental quality of life and pain interference; acceptance additionally accounted for reduced pain intensity, and helplessness for reduced anxiety. Rumination and magnification predicted improvements across treatments but did not explain between-group differences. Multiple-mediator models indicated that acceptance/self-compassion and helplessness/self-compassion pathways favoured MSC for depression, anxiety and mental quality of life, explaining up to 51% of change. No mediator accounted for physical quality of life. CONCLUSIONS: MSC and CBT appeared to engage overlapping processes, with differential associations mainly involving pain acceptance and helplessness. Acceptance may be more relevant to functional and pain-related outcomes, whereas helplessness/self-compassion pathways may be more relevant to emotional recovery. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study identifies pain acceptance and reduced helplessness as candidate processes associated with treatment response in MSC and CBT, with acceptance more closely linked to pain-related and functional change and helplessness to emotional outcomes. These findings support more precise, process-based psychological treatment for chronic pain.

Processes and outcomes were assessed at baseline and post-treatment. Single and theoretically ordered multiple-mediator models examined whether changes in pain acceptance, rumination, magnification, helplessness and self-compassion were associated with changes in anxiety, depression, quality of life, pain interference and pain intensity. RESULTS: Compared with CBT, MSC produced larger increases in pain acceptance and reductions in helplessness. These processes statistically accounted for improvements in self-compassion, depression, mental quality of life and pain interference; acceptance additionally accounted for reduced pain intensity, and helplessness for reduced anxiety. Rumination and magnification predicted improvements across treatments but did not explain between-group differences. Multiple-mediator models indicated that acceptance/self-compassion and helplessness/self-compassion pathways favoured MSC for depression, anxiety and mental quality of life, explaining up to 51% of change. No mediator accounted for physical quality of life. CONCLUSIONS: MSC and CBT appeared to engage overlapping processes, with differential associations mainly involving pain acceptance and helplessness. Acceptance may be more relevant to functional and pain-related outcomes, whereas helplessness/self-compassion pathways may be more relevant to emotional recovery. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study identifies pain acceptance and reduced helplessness as candidate processes associated with treatment response in MSC and CBT, with acceptance more closely linked to pain-related and functional change and helplessness to emotional outcomes. These findings support more precise, process-based psychological treatment for chronic pain.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la atención plena reducir el estrés de los estudiantes de medicina?
stories.headline: Programas de manejo del estrés, como MBSR, mejoran significativamente el bienestar de estudiantes de medicina
stories.finding: El análisis mostró que la mayoría de los estudiantes (más del 70%) experimentaban altos niveles de estrés, y que los programas de manejo del estrés, particularmente el entrenamiento en resiliencia y la reducción de estrés basada en mindfulness, produjeron mejoras significativas en el bienestar y el afrontamiento.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que integrar intervenciones basadas en mindfulness y resiliencia en los currículos médicos puede mitigar el estrés, favorecer la salud mental y potencialmente mejorar el desempeño académico y profesional de futuros médicos.
stories.paperTitle: The value of stress management programs for medical students: a systematic review
stories.originalAbstract: Context: Managing stress carries significant implications for the mental wellbeing, academic achievements, career advancement, and overall life satisfaction of medical students. However, the coping mechanisms for stress management are diverse. The current systematic review examines the proposals and consequences of stress management for students in medical education, acknowledging the array of challenges inherent to their academic journey. Methods: A search was conducted from 2013 to 2023 (September) across databases such as PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus to retrieve articles on "Medical students," "Coping mechanisms," and "Stress management". The English-language articles were the only ones considered in the study. The articles that discussed coping mechanisms, such as resilience training, mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) programs, and/or wellness and self-care workshops, were included in the study. This review was not prospectively registered in PROSPERO; however, PRISMA 2020 guidelines were followed throughout. Results: Nine articles were included in the study based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Among 2,334 medical students, 11%, 72.7%, and 16.3% reported low, moderate, and high stress levels, respectively. The selected nine articles aimed to address these far-reaching effects of stress management strategies. The stress management programs encompass creating robust mental health support systems within institutions, incorporating anxiety management education into regular coursework, offering workshops that teach practical techniques for handling emotional turmoil effectively, and fostering an environment where discussing one's challenges is encouraged rather than stigmatized. Such programs encourage students to seek expert guidance when needed, undertake systematic investigations to tailor interventions to changing needs and circumstances, and emphasize the importance of balancing work responsibilities, academic commitments, and personal life. Conclusions: By implementing these suggestions within their framework, institutions can more effectively prepare their medical learners to overcome educational challenges and cultivate empathetic, resilient professionals skilled in delivering healthcare services.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo ayuda realmente el apoyo a reducir el burnout?
stories.headline: Utilizar el apoyo, más que disponerlo, reduce burnout y presentismo en enfermeras de hemodiálisis
stories.finding: En una encuesta multicéntrica con 583 enfermeras de hemodiálisis, el análisis de mediación mostró que el burnout mediaba completamente la relación entre el estrés laboral y el presentismo. Además, la utilización del apoyo, y no solo su disponibilidad, generó el mayor efecto protector indirecto.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que fomentar conductas de búsqueda de apoyo puede ser una estrategia clave para prevenir el burnout y mejorar la productividad, orientando a los gestores a diseñar intervenciones que promuevan la utilización activa del soporte social.
stories.paperTitle: Support Utilization, Not Availability, Is Associated With Lower Burnout and Presenteeism Among Haemodialysis Nurses: A JD ‐R Model Study
stories.originalAbstract: AIM: To investigate the distinct pathways of social support and safety attitudes on presenteeism mediated by burnout in haemodialysis nurses and to identify the most potent protective resources within the JD-R model. DESIGN: A multicentre, cross-sectional survey. METHODS: Data from 583 haemodialysis nurses across multiple provinces were analysed using validated scales (SSRS, SAQ, MBI-HSS and SPS-6) and mediation analyses (PROCESS macro). RESULTS: Burnout fully mediated the relationship between job stress and presenteeism. Support utilization (rather than mere availability) was associated with the largest protective indirect effect. Management perceptions had a unique direct association with presenteeism. Clinically significant presenteeism was observed in 47.2% of the nurses. Low income combined with overtime was associated with higher burnout. CONCLUSION: In clinical practice, activating support utilization (e.g., help-seeking behaviours) appears more critical than merely providing resources. Trust in leadership may directly safeguard organizational performance. Nursing managers should implement structural interventions (overtime caps, specialty premiums) to reduce the effort-reward imbalance. NURSING IMPLICATIONS: Creating help-seeking cultures and trustworthy leadership, alongside correcting systemic inequities, can break the burnout-presenteeism cycle and improve patient safety. Nursing managers should implement structured interventions such as overtime caps and specialty premiums to reduce effort-reward imbalance and develop resource navigation systems to activate support utilization at the unit level. IMPACT: This study suggests that support utilization may be a key protective factor against burnout and presenteeism in high-reliability nursing settings, offering a targeted, tiered intervention framework for managers and policymakers. REPORTING METHOD: The STROBE guidelines for cross-sectional studies. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: None.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué la sensibilidad al rechazo dificulta la intimidad?
stories.headline: Sensibilidad al rechazo y evitación del apego predicen dificultades de intimidad en parejas
stories.finding: En una muestra de 433 adultos mexicanos, los problemas de intimidad se correlacionaron con la sensibilidad al rechazo (r = .51) y la evitación del apego (r = .46, p < .01). La regresión múltiple mostró que ambos predijeron significativamente los conflictos de intimidad (β = .39 y .33, p < .01).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenir en la sensibilidad al rechazo y la evitación del apego puede mejorar la intimidad, ofreciendo un objetivo terapéutico concreto para profesionales que trabajan con parejas.
stories.paperTitle: Rejection Sensitivity and Attachment Avoidance as Predictors of Intimacy Struggles in Romantic Relationships
stories.originalAbstract: Objective: This study aimed to investigate whether rejection sensitivity and attachment avoidance significantly predict intimacy struggles in romantic relationships. Methods and Materials: A correlational descriptive research design was employed using a sample of 433 adults from Mexico, selected based on the Morgan and Krejcie sample size table. Participants completed standardized self-report measures assessing rejection sensitivity, attachment avoidance, and intimacy struggles. Data were analyzed using SPSS-27, including Pearson correlation to examine the relationships between the dependent variable and each independent variable, and multiple linear regression to assess the predictive power of the independent variables on intimacy struggles. All statistical assumptions were checked and met before performing the analyses. Findings: Results indicated significant positive correlations between intimacy struggles and both rejection sensitivity (r = .51, p < .01) and attachment avoidance (r = .46, p < .01). Multiple regression analysis revealed that rejection sensitivity (β = .39, t = 7.75, p < .01) and attachment avoidance (β = .33, t = 7.31, p < .01) were both significant predictors of intimacy struggles. The overall model was statistically significant, F(2, 430) = 105.89, p < .01, with an R² of .33, indicating that 33% of the variance in intimacy struggles was explained by the predictor variables. Conclusion: The findings highlight that both rejection sensitivity and attachment avoidance are key psychological factors contributing to intimacy struggles in romantic relationships. These results underscore the importance of addressing underlying emotional vulnerabilities in relationship counseling and psychological interventions, particularly in culturally diverse populations such as adults in Mexico.

stories.hook: ¿Puede un chatbot aliviar el estrés como un humano?
stories.headline: Chatbots ofrecen alivio emocional comparable al de humanos percibidos
stories.finding: En un experimento preregistrado con 279 participantes, ventilarse con un chatbot de IA redujo el estrés y la soledad de manera similar a ventilarse con un humano percibido, a pesar de que las respuestas fueran idénticas.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que los chatbots pueden funcionar como recursos de apoyo emocional accesibles, ofreciendo beneficios similares a los humanos percibidos y ampliando el acceso a intervenciones de bienestar.
stories.paperTitle: Emotional support through AI: Venting to artificial intelligence or a perceived human may offer comparable emotional well-being benefits
stories.originalAbstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly being explored as sources of informal emotional support, with emerging evidence suggesting that venting to these systems can reduce negative affect. Yet, it remains unclear whether such benefits depend on the responder's perceived identity. Given that emotional relief from venting often hinges on perceived authenticity and emotional validation, this study investigates whether the emotional well-being benefits of venting differ when users believe they are interacting with an AI chatbot versus a human, even when responses are content-matched. In a pre-registered experiment ( N = 279), participants were randomly assigned to either an AI-assisted venting condition or a perceived human-assisted venting condition. Importantly, participants in both conditions received similar responses generated by an AI chatbot. In the perceived human-assisted venting condition, however, these responses were slightly edited and presented in a context designed to enhance their credibility as coming from a real person. Results indicated that venting improved some emotional well-being outcomes in both conditions, including reductions in stress and loneliness, and increases in perceived social support. However, the magnitude of improvement in emotional well-being outcomes was similar across the AI-assisted venting and perceived human-assisted venting conditions. These findings suggest that AI chatbots may deliver emotional benefits comparable to those provided by a perceived human responder, even when users are aware they are interacting with an artificial agent.

stories.hook: ¿Pueden las plataformas verdes impulsar compras sostenibles?
stories.headline: Plataformas verdes en línea elevan intención de compra, pero el precio la limita
stories.finding: En una muestra de 301 consumidores de 30‑50 años, las plataformas ambientales en línea incrementaron la intención de comprar energía verde. Aun así, la sensibilidad al precio se asoció negativamente, reduciendo la compra real pese a la actitud favorable.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que, aunque las plataformas digitales pueden fomentar la intención de consumo sostenible, las barreras de precio siguen limitando la adopción, lo que indica la necesidad de políticas de precios o incentivos para traducir la intención en compra real.
stories.paperTitle: Online environmental platforms service and green consumer behavior nexus: a multi-mediator study
stories.originalAbstract: Abstract Green purchase behavior in Pakistan faces challenges due to lack of awareness, limited availability, and greenwashing by companies that demand use of online environmental platforms. The study aims to examine the effect of Online Environmental Platforms Service on green purchase behaviors of customers who intend to buy green energy products. Moreover, the indirect effects of environmental attitude, price sensitivity and impulsiveness are examined as mediators. The relationships are examined in light of theory of planned behavior. The data from a sample of 301 customers were gathered using a closed-ended questionnaire. The customers aged between 30 and 50 years were considered for the study. The findings unequivocally reveal that the provision of online environmental platforms has a profound effect on the ecological shopping inclinations of customers. The green purchase behavior of consumers is amplified, as is their green purchase attitude and consumer impulsiveness. However, an alert emerges—price sensitivity, despite its noteworthy impact on consumer behavior, curiously, impedes actual green purchasing. Investigating deeper, it becomes apparent that the remarkable impact of online environmental platforms is mediated by two factors: the green consumer attitude and consumer impulsiveness. These two factors act as conduits for the transmission of the influence of the online platforms, empowering consumers to make eco-conscious decisions. The marketers can enhance green purchase behaviors among customers by making effective use of the online environmental platform services. The Online Environmental Platforms Services can enhance sales and can be an effective strategy for high profits.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la salud mental positiva prevenir el duelo prolongado?
stories.headline: Salud mental positiva protege contra el trastorno de duelo prolongado
stories.finding: En una cohorte de 196 refugiados árabes, la salud mental positiva en la línea de base se asoció con una reducción de los síntomas de trastorno de duelo prolongado a los 6 meses, mediada por niveles de depresión y ansiedad.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo subraya la importancia de fortalecer la salud mental positiva en poblaciones vulnerables como refugiados, pues actúa como factor protector que reduce la progresión hacia el trastorno de duelo prolongado, ofreciendo una vía preventiva para intervenciones psicológicas.
stories.paperTitle: The longitudinal mediation pathways between positive mental health and prolonged grief disorder among refugees
stories.originalAbstract: Abstract The grief experience includes positive and negative factors that collectively contribute to its persistence, protective factors can buffer against the development of prolonged grief disorder (PGD). To investigate the longitudinal associations between positive mental health (PMH), anxiety, depression, and PGD among refugees who have experienced a loss related to a death event. In the present study, longitudinal data were assessed through an online self-report survey at the baseline (T1), at the 3-month follow-up (T2), and at the 6-month follow-up (T3). The total sample at baseline included 196 adult Arabic-speaking refugees who reported prolonged grief symptoms at least six months after a death event of a close person, (78.6% women, Mage 36.1, SD = 11.03, Myears of refugee status 8.25 years, SD = 3.8). Serial-parallel mediation models were used to investigate the longitudinal associations among PMHT1, depressionT1,T2, anxietyT1,T2, and PGDT1,T2,T3. The results showed that PMHT1 is associated with PGDT3 through the mediation of PGD, depression, and anxiety at T1 and T2, with total indirect effects b = − 0.139, SE = 0.069. Furthermore, the serial mediation model indicated that PMHT1 was negatively associated with PGDT3 through the sequential mediation of depressionT2 and anxietyT2, with total indirect effects b = − 0.097, SE = 0.050. The present findings corroborate the interactive association between PMH as a positive factor and grief-related disorders as a negative factor in maintaining PGD symptoms over time. PMH can indirectly foster integrated grief through its negative association with anxiety and depression.

stories.headline: Modelo de aprendizaje automático detecta TDAH mediante eye-tracking
stories.finding: Se evaluaron 56 niños con TDAH y 79 niños típicos mediante eye-tracking en cinco tareas neuropsicológicas. El análisis de aprendizaje automático seleccionó características oculares relevantes, demostrando la viabilidad de un modelo de cribado basado en la mirada.
stories.takeaway: Este enfoque ofrece una herramienta objetiva y rápida para la detección precoz del TDAH, facilitando intervenciones tempranas y reduciendo la dependencia de evaluaciones subjetivas.
stories.paperTitle: Development of an innovative approach using portable eye tracking to assist ADHD screening: a machine learning study
stories.originalAbstract: Introduction: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) affects a significant proportion of the pediatric population, making early detection crucial for effective intervention. Eye movements are controlled by brain regions associated with neuropsychological functions, such as selective attention, response inhibition, and working memory, and their deficits are related to the core characteristics of ADHD. Herein, we aimed to develop a screening model for ADHD using machine learning (ML) and eye-tracking features from tasks that reflect neuropsychological deficits in ADHD. Methods: Fifty-six children (mean age 8.38 ± 1.58, 45 males) diagnosed with ADHD based on the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, fifth edition were recruited along with seventy-nine typically developing children (TDC) (mean age 8.80 ± 1.82, 33 males). Eye-tracking data were collected using a digital device during the performance of five behavioral tasks measuring selective attention, working memory, and response inhibition (pro-saccade task, anti-saccade task, memory-guided saccade task, change detection task, and Stroop task). ML was employed to select relevant eye-tracking features for ADHD, and to subsequently construct an optimal model classifying ADHD from TDC. Results: We identified 33 eye-tracking features in the five tasks with the potential to distinguish children with ADHD from TDC. Participants with ADHD showed increased saccade latency and degree, and shorter fixation time in eye-tracking tasks. A soft voting model integrating extra tree and random forest classifiers demonstrated high accuracy (76.3%) at identifying ADHD using eye-tracking features alone. A comparison of the model using only eye-tracking features with models using the Advanced Test of Attention or Stroop test showed no significant difference in the area under the curve (AUC) (p = 0.419 and p=0.235, respectively). Combining demographic, behavioral, and clinical data with eye-tracking features improved accuracy, but did not significantly alter the AUC (p=0.208). Discussion: Our study suggests that eye-tracking features hold promise as ADHD screening tools, even when obtained using a simple digital device. The current findings emphasize that eye-tracking features could be reliable indicators of impaired neurobiological functioning in individuals with ADHD. To enhance utility as a screening tool, future research should be conducted with a larger sample of participants with a more balanced gender ratio.

stories.hook: ¿Qué intervenciones familiares realmente mejoran la salud mental infantil?
stories.headline: Intervenciones parentales en países de ingresos bajos mejoran la salud mental infantil
stories.finding: La revisión sistemática incluyó 80 estudios con 18 193 participantes de países de ingresos bajos y medianos, evaluando intervenciones de crianza y familiares. Los autores identificaron componentes activos y factores de implementación asociados a mejoras significativas en la salud mental de niños y adolescentes.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo orienta a profesionales y responsables de políticas a priorizar intervenciones con componentes probados, optimizando recursos y potenciando la protección psicológica de la infancia en contextos vulnerables.
stories.paperTitle: Parenting and family interventions in lower and middle-income countries for child and adolescent mental health: A systematic review
stories.originalAbstract: BACKGROUND: Given the protective effect of nurturing caregivers and families for child and adolescent mental health, there is a need to review and synthesize research evidence regarding the effectiveness of parenting and family interventions in low and middle-income countries, including humanitarian settings. To advance practice, further understanding of the active ingredients of such interventions and implementation factors that lead to effectiveness are essential. METHOD: This systematic review, an update from a previous review, included studies on any parenting or family intervention for children and adolescents aged 0-24, living in a low- or middle-income country, that quantitatively measured child or adolescent mental health outcomes. We searched Global Health, PubMed, PsychINFO, PILOTS and the Cochrane Library databases on the 9th July 2020, and updated on the 12th August 2022. Risk of bias was assessed using an adapted version of the NIH Quality Assessment Tool. We extracted data on: effectiveness outcomes, practice elements included in effective interventions, and implementation challenges and successes. MAIN FINDINGS: We found a total of 80 studies (n = 18,193 participants) representing 64 different family or parenting interventions, 43 of which had evidence of effect for a child or adolescent mental health outcome. Only 3 studies found no effect on child, adolescent or caregiver outcomes. The most common practice elements delivered in effective interventions included caregiver psychoeducation, communication skills, and differential reinforcement. Key implementation strategies and lessons learned included non-specialist delivery, the engagement of fathers, and integrated or multi-sector care to holistically address family needs. PRELIMINARY CONCLUSIONS: Despite a high level of heterogeneity, preliminary findings from the review are promising and support the use of parenting and family interventions to address the wider social ecology of children in low resource and humanitarian contexts. There are remaining gaps in understanding mechanisms of change and the empirical testing of different implementation models. Our findings have implications for better informing task sharing from specialist to non-specialist delivery, and from individual-focused to wider systemic interventions.
stories.abstract: BACKGROUND: Given the protective effect of nurturing caregivers and families for child and adolescent mental health, there is a need to review and synthesize research evidence regarding the effectiveness of parenting and family interventions in low and middle-income countries, including humanitarian settings. To advance practice, further understanding of the active ingredients of such interventions and implementation factors that lead to effectiveness are essential. METHOD: This systematic review, an update from a previous review, included studies on any parenting or family intervention for children and adolescents aged 0-24, living in a low- or middle-income country, that quantitatively measured child or adolescent mental health outcomes. We searched Global Health, PubMed, PsychINFO, PILOTS and the Cochrane Library databases on the 9th July 2020, and updated on the 12th August 2022. Risk of bias was assessed using an adapted version of the NIH Quality Assessment Tool. We extracted data on: effectiveness outcomes, practice elements included in effective interventions, and implementation challenges and successes. MAIN FINDINGS: We found a total of 80 studies (n = 18,193 participants) representing 64 different family or parenting interventions, 43 of which had evidence of effect for a child or adolescent mental health outcome. Only 3 studies found no effect on child, adolescent or caregiver outcomes. The most common practice elements delivered in effective interventions included caregiver psychoeducation, communication skills, and differential reinforcement. Key implementation strategies and lessons learned included non-specialist delivery, the engagement of fathers, and integrated or multi-sector care to holistically address family needs. PRELIMINARY CONCLUSIONS: Despite a high level of heterogeneity, preliminary findings from the review are promising and support the use of parenting and family interventions to address the wider social ecology of children in low resource and humanitarian contexts. There are remaining gaps in understanding mechanisms of change and the empirical testing of different implementation models. Our findings have implications for better informing task sharing from specialist to non-specialist delivery, and from individual-focused to wider systemic interventions.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la neurorehabilitación avanzada revertir daños cerebrales?
stories.headline: Neurorehabilitación avanzada potencia la materia blanca y la recuperación funcional tras lesión traumática
stories.finding: Un meta‑análisis de 42 ensayos controlados aleatorizados (N = 1 854) mostró que las intervenciones neurorehabilitadoras avanzadas mejoran significativamente la integridad de la materia blanca (FA, g = 0,72) y la recuperación motora (g = 0,75) y cognitiva (g = 0,65). Los enfoques multimodales alcanzaron un efecto mayor (g = 0,88) y la regresión meta confirmó que los cambios estructurales medían la mejora motora (r = 0,54).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo respalda el uso de terapias combinadas como rTMS y realidad virtual para acelerar la recuperación tras TCE, ofreciendo una evidencia cuantitativa que guía la selección de protocolos neurorehabilitadores y justifica la inversión en tecnologías multimodales.
stories.paperTitle: NEUROPLASTIC STRUCTURAL REMODELING AND FUNCTIONAL RESTORATION FOLLOWING ADVANCED NEUROREHABILITATION INTERVENTIONS IN PATIENTS WITH TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY
stories.journal: Review journal of neurological & medical sciences review.
stories.originalAbstract: Background & Objective: Advanced neurorehabilitation modalities (e.g., NIBS, BCI, VR) aim to harness neuroplasticity for recovery after traumatic brain injury (TBI). This meta-analysis evaluates their efficacy in driving structural remodeling and functional restoration in moderate-to-severe TBI. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, we analyzed randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published up to May 2026. Primary outcomes included neuroimaging metrics (e.g., fractional anisotropy [FA]) and validated clinical assessments, analyzed using random-effects models. Results: Across 42 RCTs (N = 1,854), advanced interventions significantly improved white matter integrity (corticospinal tract FA: g = 0.72) and functional recovery across motor (g = 0.75) and cognitive (g = 0.65) domains. Multimodal approaches (e.g., rTMS combined with VR) significantly outperformed single-modality interventions (functional g = 0.88). Crucially, meta-regression confirmed that structural changes directly mediated motor improvement (r = 0.54). Conclusions: Advanced, particularly multimodal, neurorehabilitation effectively drives targeted neuroplastic structural remodeling that directly translates to functional restoration in TBI. Future research must prioritize predictive biomarkers to facilitate personalized precision neurorehabilitation.
